cons.claim: A generous callback rule can be used by a small number of customers in ways that make accounts unprofitable for the operator
cons.example: monthly return visits requested on a quarterly programme for pressure the service was never going to eliminate

cons.claim: Routing without adjudicating means the seller sometimes passes on requests they know fall outside coverage
cons.example: forwarding a wildlife or bird complaint the programme never covered and absorbing the operator's irritation

failure_modes: arguing coverage with the customer at the moment of complaint
having no agreed response window, so urgency is negotiated per incident
never learning that callbacks occurred and losing the pattern entirely
treating every callback as a service failure when some are expectation failures the seller created
acceptance_tests: the callback qualification criteria, contact route, response window and cost bearer are written into the partnership terms and reflected in what customers are told
callback events reach the seller and are reviewed for pattern at a defined cadence
revisit_triggers: callback volume shifts materially by season, seller or technician
the operator changes its response commitment or cost position
customers report confusion about how to request a return visit

base.update_signal: callback volume or composition shifts, or the operator changes its response window or cost position

nodes.definition: Have a written path, known before it is ever needed, for the events that must never be improvised: a customer reporting illness, irritation or an exposure concern after a service; a pet, aquarium or non-target animal harmed; property damage or staining; an allegation that an application was made improperly or by an unlicensed person; or a customer claiming the sale itself was deceptive. In every one of these the seller's role is identical: record what was said with times and the customer's own words, notify the licensed operator immediately through a route that does not depend on anyone's availability, direct medical questions to medical professionals and to poison-control resources rather than answering them, never diagnose or speculate about cause, never dispose of or alter anything that might be evidence, never offer a settlement or any assurance about liability or coverage, and never discourage a customer from contacting the regulator. The operator, their insurer and the regulator own the resolution; the seller owns fast, accurate and honest reporting.

included: the incident classes that trigger the path
excluded: determining cause or liability
medical or veterinary advice
insurance coverage interpretation
communicating with a regulator on the operator's behalf

pros.claim: A path written in advance produces the right behaviour in the ten minutes when improvisation does the most damage
pros.example: a seller receiving an illness report and recording it verbatim, referring the caller to medical and poison-control resources and notifying the operator within the hour rather than reassuring the customer it was harmless

pros.claim: Honest, fast reporting is what keeps the seller a credible partner after something goes wrong, which is when partnerships are actually tested
pros.example: the operator learning of a pet incident from the seller rather than from a regulator's enquiry

cons.claim: Escalating immediately can strain the partnership and will sometimes escalate an event that would have resolved itself
cons.example: an operator irritated by a formal notification about staining that a return visit would have handled

cons.claim: Refusing to reassure a frightened customer feels cold in the moment and can read as evasion of responsibility
cons.example: declining to say the product is harmless to a parent asking directly about their child

failure_modes: reassuring a customer about health effects the seller is not qualified to assess
delaying notification to see whether the problem resolves itself
offering compensation or admitting fault on the operator's behalf
discouraging a customer from contacting the regulator to protect the relationship
acceptance_tests: a written escalation path exists naming the incident classes, the immediate notification route and the referral destinations for medical questions
every incident produces a verbatim dated record and an operator notification with a timestamp
no record shows the seller offering settlement, assigning cause, or discouraging regulator contact
revisit_triggers: any incident occurs, whatever its outcome
the operator changes its notification route or insurer
a regulator issues guidance on complaint or incident reporting

base.update_signal: an incident occurs, the operator changes insurer or notification route, or regulator guidance on incident reporting changes

nodes.definition: On a set cadence, review the partnership against the evidence the earlier loops produced: the initial-service on-time rate, callback rate by pest class and by seller, complaint and incident history, licence and insurance standing at the last verification, statement accuracy and payment timeliness, and the chargeback pattern, including the uncomfortable half of it, which is whether chargebacks cluster around one seller's own over-promising rather than around the operator's delivery. The output is a decision rather than a feeling: continue as is, renegotiate specific terms such as capacity commitments, callback cost bearing or residual continuation, tighten the seller's own promise discipline, or exit, and if exit, work out what the written ownership terms mean for the accounts already on the books. Reviewing the partner without reviewing your own selling turns the exercise into blame-shifting and discards the half of the data you actually control.

included: the review metric set and its cadence
the continue, renegotiate, tighten or exit decision
what exit means for accounts already written
excluded: valuing the account book, which the recurring-contracts knowledge base owns
legal steps in a separation
the operator's internal performance management

pros.claim: A cadence review converts scattered irritations into a decision made on evidence rather than on the most recent bad week
pros.example: a review showing that on-time rate is fine and that callbacks track one seller's result-timeline language, which changes the fix entirely

pros.claim: Including self-review keeps the partnership survivable, because most fixable problems are shared
pros.example: tightening what is promised about start dates instead of demanding capacity the operator was never going to add

cons.claim: Reviews are only as good as the underlying records, and a season of thin verification produces a review that measures nothing
cons.example: a review with no first-service data that reduces to an argument about impressions

cons.claim: Raising performance issues with a partner who holds the licence and the accounts carries real relationship risk
cons.example: a small referral partner unable to press an operator who could simply stop taking their accounts

failure_modes: reviewing the partner and never the seller's own promises
holding the review without the on-time, callback, incident and statement data
deciding to exit without checking what the ownership terms do to accounts already written
letting the review lapse in the seasons when the data would matter most
acceptance_tests: each review runs on a defined cadence with the on-time rate, callback pattern, incident history, licence standing and statement accuracy in front of it
each review records an explicit decision and, where exit is considered, the ownership consequence for existing accounts
revisit_triggers: the review cadence date arrives
an incident, licence lapse or statement dispute occurs
chargebacks or callbacks shift materially in either direction

base.update_signal: review-cadence data shows a sustained shift in on-time rate, callbacks, incidents, licence standing or statement accuracy

edges.why_related: the line between selling and performing can only be drawn once the credential classes and who must hold them are mapped
the map defines the questions the verification loop must take to the regulator and re-verify on cadence
which structures are available depends on what the seller may lawfully do themselves versus what a licensed party must do
partner verification is an instance of the verification loop, using the regulator lookup and the dated log
the ownership questions that must be answered in writing are set by which structure was chosen
whether residuals survive and for how long is an ownership term before it is a pay mechanism
capacity can only be assessed for the classes and jurisdictions the verified licence actually covers
knowing what each pest class needs is what makes a walkthrough look for the right evidence in the right places
a finding can only be shown if a structured walkthrough produced a located, photographed observation
approach classes are only meaningful when tied to the behaviour of the pest class they target
the prevention framing is assembled out of the approach classes, including the non-chemical ones
understanding what an approach class involves is what lets a seller recognise which promises the label would govern
occupant, pet and site screening exists because label restrictions and re-entry conditions turn on exactly those facts
the packet names the licensed servicer and tells the customer how to verify them, which requires the diligence file to exist
vulnerable-buyer practice is the disclosure duty intensified, checking understanding rather than merely delivering information
the ledger records the specific commitments made on top of the standard disclosure at this particular sale
the packet cannot convey what was promised unless the promises were written down at the sale
the scheduling constraints carried in the handoff are only credible if they came from a verified capacity window
verification compares what was delivered against what the packet said was promised and required
the first check is where most callbacks originate and where the protocol is first exercised
the screening record is the first thing an incident report is read against, so the path depends on screening having happened
the on-time and experience data that makes a review evidence-based comes from first-service checks
nothing may be written into the ledger that would require an application the label does not permit
edges.benefit_of_coupling: the ledger becomes a filter that catches unlawful promises before they reach the technician
edges.risk_of_conflict: a seller records a customer-pleasing commitment the applicator must then refuse

edges.why_related: findings may describe what was observed but must stop short of the determination only a credentialed party may make
edges.benefit_of_coupling: observations stay useful to the customer while diagnosis stays with the licensed inspector
edges.risk_of_conflict: a confident observation is heard as a diagnosis the customer acts on

edges.why_related: the handoff is incomplete, and the service must not be scheduled, until the occupancy and pet answers ride with it
edges.benefit_of_coupling: the applicator makes their method decision with the household facts in hand
edges.risk_of_conflict: a fast handoff omits the screening answers in order to hit a scheduling window

edges.why_related: only verified regulatory statements may appear in the packet; unverified ones are removed rather than softened
edges.benefit_of_coupling: the customer-facing document never asserts a rule the business has not confirmed
edges.risk_of_conflict: a plausible but unverified claim about rights or requirements survives into print

edges.why_related: pay that is earned per account rewards writing more accounts now, while capacity limits how many can be serviced as promised
edges.resolution_rule: the verified capacity window wins: promises are made only inside it, and if commission pressure argues for selling past it, selling in that area pauses until capacity exists
edges.risk_of_conflict: accounts written beyond capacity return as missed first services, cancellations and chargebacks

edges.why_related: per-account pay rewards the close, and the fastest close is often the one that overstates what was found
edges.resolution_rule: evidence discipline dominates absolutely: no finding is stated beyond what is documented, and a sale lost to an honest uncertainty is recorded as a correct outcome rather than a miss
edges.risk_of_conflict: an inflated finding becomes a complaint that reaches the operator's licence

edges.why_related: when a customer is upset and the technician is days out, the seller is tempted to handle the problem personally
edges.resolution_rule: the credential line holds without exception: the seller may inspect, document, escalate and communicate, and may never apply anything, however small the problem or however long the wait
edges.risk_of_conflict: a helpful unlicensed application exposes the operator's licence and the seller personally

edges.why_related: customers want an elimination promise written down, while the honest framing manages pressure to a threshold
edges.resolution_rule: threshold language wins: no eradication or pest-free promise is recorded or spoken, and the ledger instead records the visit rhythm, what recurrence looks like and how a callback is requested
edges.risk_of_conflict: a written elimination promise guarantees a dispute the service can never satisfy

edges.why_related: same-visit closing devices raise per-visit yield while the care rules require slowing down exactly those sales
edges.resolution_rule: consent quality dominates: when any vulnerability trigger is present the sale slows, urgency devices are dropped, and walking away is treated as the correct commercial outcome
edges.risk_of_conflict: a pressured sale to a vulnerable buyer becomes a rescission, a complaint and a reputational problem

edges.why_related: capacity shortfalls are the mechanism that produces missed initial-service windows, which is what verification detects
who the incident is notified to, and which insurer and licence stand behind the resolution, is determined by the diligence file
findings are shown first so that the disclosure and the agreement are made against an understood picture rather than a claim
the credential classes must be mapped before a partner's licence can be checked against the services to be sold
callback patterns reveal which promises were unrealistic and retune what gets recorded and said at the next sale
observed completion timing is the only honest input to the next capacity statement and its promise constraint
the review decision can force a renegotiation or an exit, which reopens the structure and ownership choices
every incident tests the screening questions and usually adds one that was not being asked
both are structured pre-sale information-gathering routines whose recorded output the licensed party relies on

conflict_axes.name: licence_certainty_versus_speed_to_revenue
conflict_axes.description: Verifying every credential class and partner standing before selling delays revenue, while starting now and sorting licensing later is how unlicensed practice happens.
poles: verify every credential class and partner standing first
start selling now and resolve licensing as it comes up
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: licensing verification is a hard gate, not a parallel task: no account is written in a class or jurisdiction whose credential row is unverified

conflict_axes.name: asset_ownership_versus_ease_of_entry
conflict_axes.description: The structures that require no licence, no insurance and no capital are the ones that leave the seller owning nothing when the partnership ends.
poles: own the licensed operation and the customer contracts
stay a light referral partner with no infrastructure
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: decide by book intent: if the goal is a durable recurring asset, either carry the heavier structure or negotiate explicit ownership and residual terms before volume exists

conflict_axes.name: sales_velocity_versus_service_capacity
conflict_axes.description: Per-account pay pushes volume forward while technician hours, route coverage and seasonal backlog set a hard ceiling on what can be delivered as promised.
poles: write every account available now
sell only what the verified capacity window can service
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the capacity window governs the promise; when demand exceeds it, either the promise changes or selling in that area pauses, never both stay optimistic

conflict_axes.name: urgency_that_closes_versus_evidence_that_holds
conflict_axes.description: Fear closes pest-control sales faster than anything else, and it is the one lever that cannot be pulled honestly without evidence behind it.
poles: heighten urgency to close today
state only the urgency the documented evidence supports
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: documented evidence sets the ceiling on urgency language; where there is nothing to show, prevention is sold on its own merits or nothing is sold

conflict_axes.name: helpful_expertise_versus_credential_boundary
conflict_axes.description: A well-read seller often knows enough to answer the customer's question, and answering it can be the act that crosses into unlicensed practice.
poles: answer the customer fully and be useful
defer every determination and application to the licensed party
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: describe classes, mechanisms and observations freely; never identify definitively, prescribe, or apply, and route the question with a named next step so deferral reads as competence

conflict_axes.name: eradication_promise_versus_threshold_truth
conflict_axes.description: Customers want to be told the pests will be gone, and integrated pest management can only honestly offer managed pressure in an open environment.
poles: promise the outcome the customer wants to hear
explain thresholds, recurrence and monitoring
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: threshold language is non-negotiable in speech, script and ledger; the compensating move is explaining what recurrence looks like and how a callback works, not softening the promise

conflict_axes.name: customer_request_versus_label_constraint
conflict_axes.description: Customers ask for interior treatments, specific rooms, specific frequencies and shortcuts around re-entry that the product label may not permit.
poles: accommodate the request to win the account
promise only what the label and the applicator can support
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the label governs; the request is routed to the applicator as a question rather than accepted as a commitment, and the customer is told that is what is happening

conflict_axes.name: disclosure_completeness_versus_conversation_flow
conflict_axes.description: Every exclusion, preparation duty and cancellation right disclosed before signature is also an exit the hesitant buyer can take.
poles: keep the conversation simple and close
disclose role, exclusions and cancellation before consent
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: disclosure before signature is a floor, not a variable; simplify by improving how it is said, never by removing what is said

conflict_axes.name: partner_loyalty_versus_customer_protection
conflict_axes.description: When the operator is the source of the problem, the seller's income depends on the relationship they may need to report or leave.
poles: protect the partnership that pays you
protect the customer and the record
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: customer safety and regulatory honesty dominate; the incident path runs whatever it costs the relationship, and the review decides the partnership afterwards on the evidence

conflict_axes.name: documentation_burden_versus_field_speed
conflict_axes.description: Photographs, screening answers, ledgers and handoff packets all consume the same minutes that would otherwise be spent in front of the next prospect.
poles: maximise conversations per selling hour
document every finding, answer and promise at the point of sale
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: documentation happens at the moment of the sale or it does not happen honestly; the correct adjustment is fewer, better-documented conversations rather than retrospective reconstruction

edge_cases.description: A homeowner insists they have seen termites and wants treatment today, while the partner operator holds only a general-pest endorsement
edge_cases.trigger: a lead arrives in a pest class outside the partner's verified categories and the customer is urgent
edge_cases.mitigation: state that only a credentialed inspection can determine wood-destroying organisms, refer to a properly endorsed inspector, and sell nothing against an undetermined finding

edge_cases.description: The partner operator's licence or insurance lapses mid-season while accounts are already on the books
edge_cases.trigger: a renewal watch entry or a licensee lookup shows an expired or suspended credential
edge_cases.mitigation: stop writing accounts immediately, notify customers with scheduled service, confirm status with the regulator, and resume only on documented reinstatement

edge_cases.description: The property has a beehive behind the fence, a koi pond, or an aquarium in the room the customer wants treated
edge_cases.trigger: screening or the walkthrough reveals non-target organisms sensitive to application nearby
edge_cases.mitigation: record the detail precisely, make no promise about method or area, and pass it to the operator as a determination the applicator must make against the label

edge_cases.description: A customer calls the seller reporting a headache and nausea after the initial service and asks whether the product is dangerous
edge_cases.trigger: a post-service health or exposure concern is reported to the sales side rather than the operator
edge_cases.mitigation: record the report verbatim with times, refer medical questions to medical professionals and poison-control resources, notify the operator immediately, and offer no assessment of cause or safety

edge_cases.description: An adult child calls the day after a sale alleging their elderly parent was pressured into a recurring agreement
edge_cases.trigger: a third party challenges the consent quality of a completed sale
edge_cases.mitigation: honour cancellation without argument, review the disclosure and ledger record for what was actually said, and treat the event as a practice signal rather than a customer problem

edge_cases.description: A tenant signs a recurring agreement for a property the landlord owns and manages
edge_cases.trigger: the person consenting may lack authority to authorise service or to bind the property
edge_cases.mitigation: ask the authority-to-authorise question before agreement, record the answer, and route multi-unit or landlord-controlled properties to the operator to confirm notification duties

edge_cases.description: During a sales visit the customer asks the seller to knock down a wasp nest or spray a visible trail while they are there
edge_cases.trigger: a customer requests an on-the-spot application from an unlicensed seller
edge_cases.mitigation: decline with the prepared script naming who will do it and when, book the licensed technician, and never perform even a small free application

edge_cases.description: A seasonal demand wave pushes initial services well past the window customers were promised
edge_cases.trigger: verified capacity is exceeded by accounts already sold
edge_cases.mitigation: pause selling in the affected area, contact every affected customer before they notice the slip, and refresh the capacity statement before promising again

edge_cases.description: The operator asks the seller to carry granules or leave product with customers to help between visits
edge_cases.trigger: the partner proposes a task that would put product in the seller's or the customer's hands
edge_cases.mitigation: decline in writing, note it in the partnership record, and raise it at the next review as a boundary the partnership must respect

edge_cases.description: A customer calls three days after the initial visit angry that they still see ants, on a programme built around baiting
edge_cases.trigger: the result timeline of the approach class was compressed or omitted at the sale
edge_cases.mitigation: route the callback rather than debating it, then check whether the ledger and script set an honest timeline and correct the language before the next selling day

edge_cases.description: The partnership ends and the operator asserts that every account, contract and address record belongs to them
edge_cases.trigger: separation occurs without written ownership terms, or with terms nobody read
edge_cases.mitigation: work from the written terms if they exist, take legal advice if they do not, and treat the episode as the reason ownership answers precede volume in any future partnership

edge_cases.description: A childcare centre or food-service site accepts a proposal that carries notification or posting duties the seller was unaware of
edge_cases.trigger: a special-status site enters the pipeline without a verified notification answer
edge_cases.mitigation: flag the site class to the operator before any scheduling promise, take the notification question through the verification loop, and hold the account until the answer is recorded

workflow.action: Map the credential classes for every service you intend to sell
workflow.description: Build the jurisdictional map of firm licence, applicator certification and category endorsements, supervised-technician tiers and any seller-side registration, one row per service
workflow.artifact: jurisdictional credential map with verification source and date per row
workflow.gate: every service in the intended offer has a named credential class, a named holder and a dated regulator source, and unresolved rows are marked unverified and excluded from the offer

workflow.action: Draw the sell-versus-apply line and write the not-doing list
workflow.description: Classify each field activity as sales or application, write the refusal list with escalation targets, and prepare the decline script
workflow.artifact: boundary list with escalation targets and decline script
workflow.gate: each listed activity names the licensed party it routes to and the seller-registration question carries a dated regulator answer

workflow.action: Stand up the verification loop and its log
workflow.description: Establish primary-source verification with dated entries and re-verification intervals, and adopt the rule that unverified means do not sell against it
workflow.artifact: dated regulatory verification log with next-review dates
workflow.gate: every compliance claim the business relies on has a log entry with source, date and re-verification date

workflow.action: Choose the partnering structure and write its implications
workflow.description: Select among owning the licensed operation, salesperson, referral partner and branded reseller, and answer the licence, servicer, ownership and money-flow axes explicitly
workflow.artifact: structure decision memo answering all four axes
workflow.gate: the memo states who holds the licence, who performs the service, who owns the account and how money moves, and the assumed credential position matches a verified map row

workflow.action: Verify the partner operator and set the renewal watch
workflow.description: Check licence status and categories, responsible-charge individual, insurance and bond, and the public disciplinary record, then diarise expiries
workflow.artifact: dated operator diligence file with expiry calendar
workflow.gate: active licence with categories covering every service to be sold, in-force insurance sighted, disciplinary record checked, expiries diarised with lead time

workflow.action: Settle account ownership and the commission mechanism in writing
workflow.description: Drive the ownership questions and the six commission-mechanism questions into the partnership agreement before volume exists, and prepare the statement reconciliation habit
workflow.artifact: partnership term sheet covering ownership, residuals, exclusivity, non-solicit and commission mechanics
workflow.gate: contract paper, billing relationship, data custody, residual continuation, exclusivity and non-solicit each have a written answer, and the earning event, base, deductions and chargeback triggers are written down

workflow.action: Confirm capacity and lead time per selling area and season
workflow.description: Establish coverage, treated pest classes, technician availability and the current initial-service window, and convert them into a promise constraint
workflow.artifact: dated capacity and lead-time statement per selling area
workflow.gate: no promise permitted in the field exceeds the current statement, and a refresh cadence is set for the season

workflow.description: Assemble pest-class behaviour and conducive conditions, the walkthrough structure and evidence vocabulary, the approach classes with their honest timelines, and the prevention framing
workflow.artifact: service literacy brief with honest outcome language per pest class
workflow.gate: each pest class carries honest outcome language and a named escalation cue to a licensed inspector, and no material contains eradication language, product names or rates

workflow.action: Screen occupancy, pets and site class before any scheduling promise
workflow.description: Ask and record the occupant, pet, sensitivity, food-area and special-status site questions at the visit, and transmit them to the operator
workflow.artifact: occupant, pet and site screening record attached to the account
workflow.gate: screening is complete and recorded before any scheduling or method promise is made, and special-status sites are flagged for operator confirmation

workflow.action: Walk the property and present findings from evidence
workflow.description: Run the perimeter, entry-point and interior walkthrough, photograph and locate what is found, present findings with stated uncertainty and no manufactured urgency
workflow.artifact: documented findings set with images and locations
workflow.gate: every stated finding has a location and image or is explicitly labelled unverified, and no health, structural or infestation claim exceeds the evidence

workflow.action: Disclose before signature, then record the promise ledger
workflow.description: Walk the customer through role, licensed servicer, coverage and exclusions, preparation and cancellation route, apply the vulnerability triggers, then write down every promise made
workflow.artifact: delivered disclosure packet plus a completed promise ledger held by customer, operator and seller
workflow.gate: the packet was delivered and walked through before signature, vulnerability triggers were applied, and the ledger names covered and excluded pests, visit rhythm, re-service meaning, preparation duties and any one-off commitment

workflow.action: Hand off to the technician, then verify the first service
workflow.description: Transmit access, findings, screening answers, promises and scheduling constraints in the channel the operator actually reads, then confirm completion with the operator and experience with the customer
workflow.artifact: handoff packet plus a recorded first-service verification with any gap routed and tracked
workflow.gate: the packet reached the technician intact before the visit, and the first-service check is recorded within the defined window with any gap routed to the operator by date

dominance_rules.rule: Licensing status dominates every revenue consideration
dominance_rules.rationale: unlicensed application or selling in an unlicensed class can end the operator's licence and the seller's business at once, which no commission offsets
dominance_rules.trigger: any doubt about whether a party holds the credential class for the work being sold or performed
dominance_rules.action: stop; write no account in that class or jurisdiction until the regulator-verified row exists

dominance_rules.rule: The pesticide label dominates any customer request or sales promise
dominance_rules.rationale: the label is legally binding on site, pest, rate, protective equipment and re-entry, and a seller cannot promise around it
dominance_rules.trigger: a request or a proposed promise implies a use the label may not permit
dominance_rules.action: make no commitment; route the request to the licensed applicator as a question and tell the customer that is what is happening

dominance_rules.rationale: invented or inflated findings are the fastest route to a complaint that reaches the regulator, and they destroy the trust a recurring service depends on
dominance_rules.trigger: a claim would go beyond what was observed and recorded
dominance_rules.action: state the uncertainty aloud and offer a credentialed inspection instead of the claim

dominance_rules.rule: Occupant, pet and non-target safety dominates schedule and close rate
dominance_rules.rationale: an exposure or animal incident is irreversible in a way that a lost sale is not
dominance_rules.trigger: occupancy, pet, sensitivity or site-class information is missing, incomplete or concerning
dominance_rules.action: make no scheduling or method promise until the answers are recorded and passed to the operator for determination

dominance_rules.rationale: a sale that a vulnerable or frightened buyer did not truly understand is worthless commercially and indefensible ethically
dominance_rules.trigger: the buyer is elderly and alone, evidently confused, working across a language barrier, or acting out of fear
dominance_rules.action: slow down, check understanding in plain language, invite a second decision-maker, surface the cancellation route, and walk away if doubt remains

dominance_rules.rationale: accounts sold beyond capacity return as missed first services, cancellations and chargebacks, and they poison the partnership
dominance_rules.trigger: the promise a seller wants to make exceeds the current verified capacity window
dominance_rules.action: promise only the verified window, or pause selling in that area until capacity exists

dominance_rules.rule: The written promise dominates anyone's memory
dominance_rules.rationale: disputes about what was said at the door are unresolvable and always end badly for the party without a record
dominance_rules.trigger: the seller and the operator disagree about what a customer was told
dominance_rules.action: the ledger governs; where it is silent, honour the customer's reasonable understanding and fix the recording gap immediately

dominance_rules.rationale: obstructing or delaying an incident report converts a service problem into a legal one and implicates the seller personally
dominance_rules.trigger: an incident, exposure claim, animal harm, or an allegation of unlicensed application or deceptive selling
dominance_rules.action: record verbatim, notify the operator immediately, refer medical questions onward, and never discourage a customer from contacting the regulator

dominance_rules.rule: Primary-source verification dominates operator assurance and industry folklore
dominance_rules.rationale: the phrase everyone does it this way has no standing with a regulator and is how compliant-looking operations become non-compliant
dominance_rules.trigger: a compliance question is answered by custom, by a competitor's practice, or by the partner's recollection
dominance_rules.action: take the question to the regulator, log the answer with its date, and suspend the practice until it is logged

dominance_rules.rule: Written ownership terms dominate optimistic partnership assumptions
dominance_rules.rationale: the recurring book is the asset, and the party holding the contract and the service data holds it regardless of who generated it
dominance_rules.trigger: account volume is being built before the ownership questions have written answers
dominance_rules.action: pause account-building until contract paper, data custody, residual continuation and separation mechanics are written into the agreement

anti_rework_rules.rule: Map credential classes before choosing a partnering structure
anti_rework_rules.prevents: building a structure, a brand and a pipeline around work nobody in the partnership is licensed to perform

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify the operator's licence categories before generating leads in a pest class
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a stream of termite, fumigation or rodent leads the partner cannot lawfully service, which must then be abandoned or given away

anti_rework_rules.rule: Settle account ownership and residual terms before writing volume
anti_rework_rules.prevents: building a route of recurring accounts that turns out to belong entirely to the operator at separation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm capacity and the current lead time before promising any start date
anti_rework_rules.prevents: missed first services, early cancellations and commission chargebacks that all trace to one optimistic sentence

anti_rework_rules.rule: Ask the occupancy, pet and sensitivity questions before proposing any treatment
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a promised plan the applicator must retract at the door, and the incident that follows when nobody retracts it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Photograph and locate findings at the moment of observation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: unprovable claims, disputed callbacks and a findings record reconstructed from memory after a complaint

anti_rework_rules.rule: Deliver the disclosure packet before the signature rather than after
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rescissions, non-disclosure complaints and the argument about who the customer thought they were buying from

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the promise ledger before the handoff leaves your hands
anti_rework_rules.prevents: the technician delivering a different service than the customer bought, and a dispute nobody can settle

anti_rework_rules.rule: Reconcile the first commission statement against the written mechanism
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a whole season of accumulated misunderstanding about earning events, deductions and residuals paid out wrongly

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the incident escalation path before any incident occurs
anti_rework_rules.prevents: improvised reassurance, delayed notification and admissions that create liability in the first ten minutes

iteration_protocol.trigger: callbacks cluster on one seller's accounts or on one pest class
iteration_protocol.action: audit the promise ledgers and findings records behind them and retune what is claimed at the door before the next selling day

iteration_protocol.trigger: the partner's licence, categories or insurance change, lapse or approach renewal
iteration_protocol.action: re-run diligence against the credential map and pause selling in any class the current categories do not cover

iteration_protocol.trigger: initial services begin landing outside the promised window
iteration_protocol.action: refresh the capacity statement, contact affected customers before they notice, and constrain field promises to the new window

iteration_protocol.trigger: an exposure, illness, animal or property incident is reported
iteration_protocol.action: run the escalation path immediately, then review the screening questions and the label-boundary claims that preceded it

iteration_protocol.trigger: a complaint alleges pressure, confusion or a vulnerable buyer
iteration_protocol.action: honour cancellation without argument, review the disclosure and consent practice against the record, and retrain the door approach

iteration_protocol.trigger: a regulator publishes a change or a verification log entry reaches its re-verification date
iteration_protocol.action: re-verify from the primary source and update the credential map and any affected customer-facing disclosure

iteration_protocol.trigger: a commission statement disagrees with the written mechanism
iteration_protocol.action: reconcile line by line, raise the discrepancy before the next cycle, and correct either the mechanism sheet or the agreement

iteration_protocol.trigger: the offer expands to a new pest class, site class or jurisdiction
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the credential map and verification loop for the new scope and extend the literacy brief before selling any of it

priority_rationale: The licensing frame comes first because nothing downstream is lawful or saleable until the credential classes, the sell-versus-apply line and a primary-source verification habit exist; the partnering block follows because structure, partner verification, ownership terms, commission mechanics and capacity determine who services the property, who owns the account and what may honestly be promised; the service-literacy and safety block sits next because a seller must be able to describe pests, inspections, treatment classes and prevention framing within label and occupant constraints before speaking to a customer at all; consent, disclosure and the promise ledger then govern the moment of agreement; and the handoff, first-service verification, callback, incident and review loops come last because they are what make the delivered service match the sold one and what turn a season of accounts into evidence for the next partnership decision.
